scenes.impact: Say it once, and Relay finds the record, the owner and the next step.

captions.text: At most companies, HR, IT,
payroll and learning each run their own portal,
with their own forms and owners.
New hires have to work out which system, form and
person applies, and support teams untangle requests
that arrive incomplete or at the wrong desk.
Relay puts all of it in one workspace,
with a Deepgram voice agent,
Nova-3 listening and Flux speaking, that
connects every service to a single conversation.
Here’s Maya, a new hire, on day one.
Relay: Hi, I'm Relay Guide.
Ask me about your onboarding, tasks, documents,
pay, benefits, or support.
Maya: What's my next highest-priority task?
Relay: Your next highest priority task is to
complete your federal and California
withholding forms.
These are due by the end of today.
Click “Complete withholding forms”
on the document just highlighted.
It reads Maya’s own records, picks the task due
first, and opens the exact form, ready to start.
Raising a concern works the same way: Relay
drafts a complete IT request for the right
team and files it when Maya confirms.
Maya: Set up a 30 minute follow-up with Casey
tomorrow afternoon at 2.
Relay: A thirty-minute follow-up with Casey Nguyen
is ready to schedule on Fri, Oct 2,
from 2:00 PM to 2:30 PM.
The subject is “Follow-up with Casey”.
It books meetings on the calendar and explains
what’s holding up a first paycheck,
and every action waits for the employee’s click.
Underneath, an intelligence layer built
for Relay gives the agent a small set
of tools to read records, open them,
highlight sections and propose actions.
The agent only names the record; Relay works
out the page and the highlight itself,
and refuses any target it doesn’t recognize.
The server decides who is signed in and gives
the agent that employee’s records alone, so each
person reaches only what they’re authorized to see.
Sensitive details, like bank numbers,
are removed before the agent ever sees them.
HR and IT see a timeline of every request,
from what was asked to the verified change.
On the real app,
103 of 110 conversations ended fully right,
and 31 of 34 spoken requests got a useful answer.
It stops talking within 51 milliseconds
when the employee cuts in,
and red-team attacks caused no unsafe actions.
Whatever the request, the employee says it once, and
Relay finds the record, the owner and the next step.

narration.text: At most companies, HR, IT, payroll and learning each run their own portal, with their own forms and owners.
New hires have to work out which system, form and person applies, and support teams untangle requests that arrive incomplete or at the wrong desk.
Relay puts all of it in one workspace, with a Deepgram voice agent, Nova-3 listening and Flux speaking, that connects every service to a single conversation.
Here’s Maya, a new hire, on day one.
It reads Maya’s own records, picks the task due first, and opens the exact form, ready to start.
Raising a concern works the same way: Relay drafts a complete IT request for the right team and files it when Maya confirms.
It books meetings on the calendar and explains what’s holding up a first paycheck, and every action waits for the employee’s click.
Underneath, an intelligence layer built for Relay gives the agent a small set of tools to read records, open them, highlight sections and propose actions.
The agent only names the record; Relay works out the page and the highlight itself, and refuses any target it doesn’t recognize.
The server decides who is signed in and gives the agent that employee’s records alone, so each person reaches only what they’re authorized to see.
Sensitive details, like bank numbers, are removed before the agent ever sees them.
HR and IT see a timeline of every request, from what was asked to the verified change.
On the real app, 103 of 110 conversations ended fully right, and 31 of 34 spoken requests got a useful answer.
